purpose: Is the depth-3 RATE-oracle collapse (run_seed's DendriticMLP, full backprop) an OPTIMIZATION wall or a GENERALIZATION collapse? Train a depth-3 rate net on the SAME compositional-inheritance task (seed 42) across hyperparameters and read TRAIN vs held-out-INHERITANCE accuracy.
interpretation: GENERALIZATION collapse, NOT an optimization wall. Every depth-3 setting that FITS the training set (train->1.000) collapses to ~chance (0.259-0.407) on held-out INHERITANCE; the 2-hidden net generalizes PERFECTLY (train 1.000, inherit 1.000); wider (192) is WORSE (0.259). The compositional-inheritance task is depth-2-SOLVABLE, so the 3rd layer is surplus capacity that memorizes a non-compositional solution. => the depth-3-ceiling absence is a TASK property (no depth-3-obligatory signal), NOT a credit failure. The depth-3 credit rung is untestable on this task; it needs a depth-3-OBLIGATORY task whose held-out generalization requires 3 composition levels (a depth-2 rate net must UNDERFIT held-out).
reproduce: SIM_BACKEND=numpy python (train DendriticMLP([n_in]+[w]*3+[k], seed=42) via research.runners._semantic_inheritance_deep_credit_derisk._train_oracle on make_task_semantic_inheritance(42, <task above>), eval _acc_on over inh_idx).
